complexity.notes: Keys come from the fixed 26-letter alphabet, so dict size is bounded at 26 and lookups are O(1) even adversarially; space is therefore O(1) under the generalized problem. The try/except around both loops is a clunky way to handle missing keys — indexing with multiset_t.get(i) (or comparing the two dicts with == directly, which is exactly multiset equality) would make the exception handling unnecessary. The second comparison loop is redundant: equal counts in one direction plus equal total lengths already imply equality, and using == on the dicts collapses both loops to one line. The bare `except:` is poor style; it swallows everything including bugs like NameError. The helper works but `multiset[i] = multiset.get(i, 0) + 1` is the idiomatic spelling.
complexity.summary: Builds a character-count dict for each string, then compares the two dicts in both directions, catching KeyError (a character present in one but missing from the other) as a non-match.
